one_line: Rival Mughal princes Dara Shukoh and Aurangzeb face off in the 1658 war of succession at Samugarh near Agra.

appearance.age_look: Both appear in their mid-30s, lean and battle-hardened, with upright royal posture and athletic builds.
appearance.face: Both have oval faces with sharp noses, neatly trimmed beards and moustaches; Dara’s complexion is slightly lighter with softer eyes and a thoughtful, almost pained default expression, while Aurangzeb’s is a shade darker with narrower, focused eyes and a cool, calculating default gaze.
appearance.hair: Both keep their hair tied up under Mughal turbans; Dara’s turban is a white, slightly conical Mughal turban wrapped with a thin pale-green band and a single small feather tucked at the side, while Aurangzeb’s is a light-cream turban with a fine gold border banded around and a subtle central turban ornament without large plumes.
appearance.costume:
Dara wears a long, knee-length, front-opening Mughal jama in soft off-white cotton with a very subtle pale-green floral print, tied to the right with a sash; over it, a sleeveless quilted light-cream brigandine-style coat with small, evenly spaced stitching hints, and a wide pale-green waist sash; he has straight, fitted churidar trousers in pale beige and soft brown leather boots; minimal jewellery—simple gold stud earrings and a thin gold chain visible at the neck.
Aurangzeb wears a slightly longer, calf-length jama in muted light-cream with fine, vertical pale-brown stripe motifs, tied to the left with a deep maroon sash; over this, a sleeveless, lightly quilted dusky-olive coat suggesting concealed armour underneath; his churidar trousers are a warm sand colour and he wears darker brown leather boots; he has no ostentatious jewellery, just a simple steel ring and a small tasbih (prayer beads) looped discreetly at his sash.
appearance.signature: Dara carries a slightly curved Mughal talwar with a simple steel hilt and a plain leather scabbard slung from his pale-green sash, while Aurangzeb carries a straight-backed talwar with a darker, almost black-brown leather scabbard and a plain cross-guard hilt at his maroon sash.

ref_desc: Depict Dara Shukoh and Aurangzeb as mid-30s Mughal princes with oval bearded faces, neat turbans, Dara in off-white and pale-green jama with light-cream quilted coat and talwar, Aurangzeb in light-cream striped jama with dusky-olive coat and maroon sash, both in brown leather boots.
sheet_prompt: Draw an anime-style full-body model sheet of two distinct Mughal princes standing side by side in 1658 battlefield attire at Samugarh. The first is Dara Shukoh: mid-30s, lean, oval face, neatly trimmed beard and moustache, slightly lighter complexion, thoughtful eyes and a pained but composed default expression. His hair is tied under a white conical Mughal turban wrapped with a thin pale-green band and a single small feather at one side. He wears a knee-length, off-white cotton jama with a very subtle pale-green floral print, fastening to the right, over slim pale-beige churidar trousers, and soft brown leather boots; over the jama is a sleeveless, light-cream quilted coat with fine, regular stitching that suggests brigandine-style padding. A wide pale-green sash cinches his waist, and from it hangs a plain leather-scabbarded curved Mughal talwar with a simple steel hilt; he has minimal jewellery, just small gold stud earrings and a thin gold chain at the neck. The second is Aurangzeb: also mid-30s, lean and wiry, slightly darker complexion, oval face with a sharp nose, neatly trimmed beard and moustache, narrow focused eyes and a cool, calculating gaze. His hair is tied beneath a light-cream turban with a fine gold border circling it and a modest central ornament, without large plumes. He wears a calf-length light-cream jama with subtle vertical pale-brown stripe motifs, fastening to the left, over warm sand-coloured churidar trousers and darker brown leather boots; over this is a sleeveless, lightly quilted dusky-olive coat that looks like it might conceal armour. A deep maroon sash at his waist supports a straight-backed talwar in a dark brown leather scabbard with a plain cross-guard hilt, and a small loop of tasbih beads hangs discreetly at the sash; the only visible jewellery is a simple steel ring. Show both characters front-on with a three-quarter turn variation to emphasize their fixed hairstyles, turbans, facial hair, exact garments and colours, along with their talwars and leather boots, keeping everything era-accurate, fully clothed, and dignified, in a clean shonen-anime line style with no background distractions.
